title: What Does This Cost Per User?
one_liner: Finance wants the cost-per-user-per-month for the AI assistant in writing, with a deadline of Friday. You don't have it yet — and you don't yet know whether it's $0.20 or $4.
brief:
## The setup

Week nine. The AI-assistant feature has been live in beta for three weeks. Today's Wednesday. The finance business partner — Henrietta Cole, sharp, ex-consultant — has emailed:

> 'Hi! Need the per-user-per-month cost for the AI assistant for Friday board prep. Including model API + vector DB + any compute. Whatever number you have is fine; we'll caveat.'

You don't have the number. You have some of the inputs (Anthropic API costs, ballparked vector DB infra) but not the per-user usage curve from production — that requires querying the logs over the three-week beta window and breaking down by user.

A defensible analysis takes about a day of work. A back-of-the-envelope number would take 30 minutes but could be off by 4×. The 'whatever number you have' framing is the trap — Henrietta will use whatever you send in front of the board on Friday, and if it's wrong by 4× it lands with the people who control the funding for next year.

You have until Friday EOD. Today is Wednesday afternoon.

## Your turn

Reply to Henrietta.
objective: Get Henrietta a defensible number by Friday. Make sure the number she takes to the board is not the 4×-wrong back-of-envelope. Show her you take the cost work seriously without making the request feel bureaucratic.
curveball: If you send back the back-of-envelope today ('roughly $1.50/user/month, with caveats') you'll be wrong by some unknown factor and Henrietta will quote whatever you sent. If you say 'I can't get you a number by Friday', Henrietta will go to Tomasz and you've ceded the cost-credibility work. The skill is what to commit to: 'I can have a defensible number for you by Friday 2pm — I want to do a proper breakdown of the actual per-user usage curve from the beta rather than ballpark it. The back-of-envelope would be ~$1.50 but could be off by 2-4× depending on the usage distribution; for board prep I'd want the real curve. Acceptable to wait until 2pm?' Henrietta will reply 'yes please, much appreciated'. Friday at 1.55pm you send a one-pager with $1.18/user/month, broken down by component, with the usage-curve assumption documented.

personas.name: Henrietta Cole
personas.position: I need a number. Defensible. By Friday
personas.fear: Taking a wrong number to the board and being the one who quoted it

green: Did not send the back-of-envelope number on Wednesday — held the line on doing it properly
Committed to a specific time (Friday 2pm) that gives Henrietta board-prep margin
Named the uncertainty explicitly in the reply — 'could be off by 2-4× ballpark'
Delivered on Friday with a one-pager: number, component breakdown, key assumption documented
yellow: Sent the back-of-envelope to be helpful — Henrietta uses it, the board sees a 4×-wrong number
Promised the analysis but missed the Friday deadline — Henrietta is now in the board with no number
Sent a number with no breakdown — board asks one question, the number unravels
Made the work look easy ('I'll send something over today') and then realised mid-analysis it's more complex
red: Sent a number rounded to 2 significant figures because the actual data wasn't ready ('$2/user/month') — overconfident on a wrong number
Forwarded the question to the senior engineer — abdicates the cost-credibility surface
Said 'we can't reliably calculate this yet' with no path forward — Henrietta goes elsewhere
Sent the number without naming the assumption ('assumes uniform usage') — the board's most likely question goes unanswered
